You asked us to move atlanticmarineinc.com from BigCommerce to Shopify. This document gives two ways to do it: Option 1 rebuilds the site on Shopify and fixes the layout problems we found (§2). Option 2 adds a full redesign on top. Both are priced at $30/hr.

Why we recommend Option 2

Option 1 fixes the structure. Option 2 is the one we'd choose, for these reasons:

It's the cheapest time to do itWe rebuild every page template during the migration anyway. The extra 20h puts a new design on pages we're already building. A redesign later means building those templates a second time.
The old look is the problemThe top of your site is a logo, a five-row menu and four ad banners (§2.1). Option 1 reorganises them, but the site still looks like the BigCommerce store in a new theme.
Your catalog is deep"Boat Outfitting" alone has 20 subcategories (§2.3), and the menu has 31 items, 19 of them product categories. Shoppers need clear browsing paths, and a designed layout does that better than a reordered one.
First impressions on mobileOn a phone, the category list fills the screen before any product (§2.3). A redesign treats mobile as the main case, not a smaller copy of desktop.
A professional first impressionCustomers judge a parts supplier by how the site looks before they trust it with a boat or RV order. A clean, modern store signals a business that is current, reliable and easy to buy from.
Better customer experienceFewer menu rows, filters beside the products, "Add to cart" on every card and product options in one row (§2) mean fewer clicks and less scrolling from search to checkout.
Higher conversion (CRO)Every step removed between landing and "Add to cart" helps more visitors finish an order. Option 2 designs the whole path for that: homepage categories, filters, cards, product page.
One consistent designHeader, cards, filters and product page are designed together, so the new site doesn't mix old patterns with new ones.
Small step up in priceOption 2 costs $600 more (20h × $30) and includes everything in Option 1.
2

What we found, and what Option 1 improves

The changes below are part of Option 1 (60h). Option 2 includes them too.

2.1 Homepage and menu

TodayThe menu takes five rows before the visitor sees anything else. The struck-out items (policies, Contact Us, About Us, Service Request, Privacy Policy) are the ones we'd remove from the main menu. Four ad banners also sit at the top, in an older header style.

TodaySearch, gift certificates, account and cart sit in a small top-right bar, away from the logo.

ReferenceA one-line header: logo, wide search ("product, brand, SKU or MPN"), account, and cart with the total. We'd use this layout with your logo.

What we'd do: keep the product categories in a single-row menu, move the minor pages to a small secondary menu above it or to the footer, and move the four banners down into a section below the header. We'd also add a category section to the homepage.

2.2 Product cards and footer

ReferenceCard with brand, price, stock status and an "Add to cart" button. We'd add the button to every card.

ReferenceEmail signup bar, then Shop, Help, Company and Visit Us columns. This is where the pages removed from the main menu would go.

2.3 Collection pages

TodayThe left column (red box) is empty on this page, and the price filter sits above the products.

TodayOn mobile the category list pushes the products far down the page.

What we'd do: put the filters in a sidebar. If we keep them above the products instead, the grid shows four products per row. On mobile the filters open as a popup.

2.4 Product page

TodayColors, voltage and finish are stacked, one choice per line, which makes the page long.

What we'd do: show the options in a horizontal row, and add a "bought together" block. We'll check Ella's built-in block first (§4).

3

Features

3.1 Brands page

Your brands page will be one page listing all brands. It will not paginate the way the Ella demo store's brand page does.

3.2 Wishlist and compare

Your site uses both. Ella includes them, so there is no extra cost on this theme. On another theme, custom code is 15h, or we set up an app for you free of charge (the app subscription is yours).

3.3 Products with many options

Many of your products have several options. Shopify supports 3 options per product. If a product has 4, we'd use an app for it. You pay the app's ongoing subscription fee, and we set the app up for you.
